A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IterResearch and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The renamed title and conference formatting do not prevent matching the method, experiments, and supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training and paradigm ablations, interaction-scaling experiments, prompting comparisons, and training dynamics.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds per-benchmark measurements of generated-token use in Appendix C.4.

M1.justification: The reconstructed workspace, evolving report, tools, decision sequence, geometric reward discounting, adaptive downsampling, and GSPO objective remain unchanged. The revised MDP description and explicit closing statements in Algorithm 1 clarify the existing procedure rather than introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training-data sources and evaluate HLE, BrowseComp, BrowseComp-zh, GAIA, Xbench-DeepSearch, and SEAL-0. The token-cost analysis uses these retained benchmarks; the added AlphaEvolve discussion is not an evaluated task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparator membership, Table 2 retains the GSPO, SFT, and Mono-Agent comparisons, and Figure 4 retains ReAct comparisons using o3 and DeepSeek-V3.1. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix C.4 adds average generated-token use as a supplementary evaluation metric, counting Think and Report tokens while excluding tool responses. Existing accuracy metrics, training settings, interaction limits, and the 200-question BrowseComp scaling subset remain unchanged. The new baseline-source disclosure does not establish a revised experimental procedure.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 adds an analysis of computational expenditure across benchmarks, contrasting BrowseComp and BrowseComp-zh with the other tasks. Existing methodology ablations, transfer experiments, interaction scaling, training dynamics, and the HLE case study are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 adds ± values to all six IterResearch scores, such as 37.3 ± 0.7 for BrowseComp and 72.8 ± 2.3 for GAIA. Neither their statistical meaning nor an associated evaluation run count is specified. This establishes new uncertainty reporting, not an established increase in runs.

E6.justification: New Table 7 reports average generated-token counts: HLE 31,426; BrowseComp 376,349; BrowseComp-zh 81,136; GAIA 33,198; Xbench-DS 31,600; and SEAL-0 28,186. The original accuracy values in Tables 1–2 and plotted results in Figures 1, 3, 4, and 5 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1.1 revises the formal specification to include reward R explicitly and represent policy decisions and environmental responses probabilistically, with reconstruction deterministic conditional on those outputs. It also replaces the unqualified Markov-property characterization with MDP-inspired language. Appendix B's discounting and complexity derivations remain unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the formalization and novelty framing: an extended-MDP formulation becomes an MDP-inspired architecture, and EAPO becomes a training strategy adapting standard discounting rather than a newly developed reinforcement-learning framework. The main performance, interaction-scaling, transfer, and prompting claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C.4 newly interprets token-use differences as task-complexity differences and argues that gains do not arise from uncontrolled expenditure, without providing comparable baseline costs. Appendix A adds an interpretation of similarity to AlphaEvolve as convergence on a general architecture for long-horizon reasoning.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 newly states that prompting-baseline scores were sourced from original publications because optimized prompts were unavailable, although its Table 1/ReAct reference is confusing. The front-page Code link changes from Alibaba-NLP/DeepResearch to Chen-GX/IterResearch. Existing hyperparameters, tool specifications, and substantive prompt instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a substantive architectural comparison with AlphaEvolve. Section 3.2 credits standard episodic discounting to Sutton and Barto, replacing the Bellman citation; ReForm and Tongyi DeepResearch are also newly cited. These are limited additions and attribution refinements within the retained research positioning.

P1.justification: The title changes to emphasize interaction scaling, and portions of the abstract, introduction, and formalism are rewritten. v2 adds acknowledgments, an AlphaEvolve paragraph, and Appendix C.4, and switches to author–year citations. Most exposition, section order, and appendix content remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 7, enlarges and relocates Figure 3, revises Figure 2's caption, and adjusts Table 1's display to accommodate uncertainty values. ICLR typography, running headers, and altered spacing reflow the document, while the existing figures and table organization are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The new token-cost measurements, baseline-source disclosure, and clearer attribution to standard reinforcement learning modestly improve transparency and positioning. Benefits are limited: the new ± values are undefined, and the cost analysis overreaches in excluding expenditure as an explanation without comparative costs. Both versions also retain the disagreement between Figure 3's scaling values and the accompanying prose.
